R-8 ('Evidence-gated cutover and actual shipment') is the single bar carrying evidencePlane='deployed'. The deployed-only property is: the managed-capability RESTRICTIONS are actually ACTIVE in the shipped build serving real sessions, verified on that build, plus the shipped plan status that follows it. This is final-shipment verification, which is the canonical deployed-only category.\n\nWHY STAGING/CURRENT-BUILD CANNOT EXERCISE IT. Staging cannot exercise this property because the property is not 'does the code work' but 'is the restriction in force in the build that real agents are actually running'. A staging or current-build run exercises a build nobody is governed by, so a pass there is silent on whether any live session is confined; staging is unable to distinguish 'the cutover works' from 'the cutover is in force'. That distinction is the whole point of an evidence-GATED cutover: R-8 exists precisely to stop a restriction being called active on the strength of a run against a build that is not serving anyone. D-018 already ruled this bar correctly specified and refused to relax it to a tree/staging plane.\n\nSCOPE OF THE WAIT (deliberately narrow). It used the same two passages, current catalog, eight singleton pairs, CPU/q8 model, warm worker, 4000 ms deadline, cache disabled and sidecar concurrency six. No CPU, memory, contention or provider explanation is asserted.\n\n## Focused diagnostic repair\n\nThe outer enqueue timer covers Governor.admit, including bounded transaction acquisition/setup, advisory locks, cutover-latch initialization, canonical and legacy identity checks, optional tenant/coalescing work, INSERT and commit.\n\nRoot cause of the diagnostic gap: PgAdmissionLedgerQueueStore.enqueue did not supply the phase getter already supported by boundedOrgTxn. A PostgreSQL timeout therefore lost the failing internal step, although targeted transitions such as mark-running already provided that attribution.\n\nThe repair extends that existing mechanism with enqueue phases for locking, the cutover latch, identity checks, tenant admission, coalescing, INSERT, race rechecks and transaction commit. It preserves query order, atomicity and admission policy.
